title: 240,000 plastic particles in 1 litre of bottled water.
accent: You can't see them. They are there.

title: Columbia University, 2024
body: Bottled water from 3 popular US brands was tested.
A new laser microscope (SRS) identifies each particle one by one, and tells which plastic it is.

title: 110,000 to 370,000
body: That is 10–100 times more than earlier estimates.
A 2018 study found 325 per litre on average. The difference is simple: we couldn't see the smallest ones before.

title: About 90% of the particles
body: Microplastic: from 5 mm down to 1 micrometre.
Nanoplastic: smaller than 1 micrometre. A human hair is roughly 50–100 times thicker.
So small that scientists are studying whether they pass through the gut and lungs into the blood.

title: The filter and the bottle itself
body: The most common was polyamide (a type of nylon), likely from plastic filters used to purify the water.
PET comes from the bottle: squeezing it, heat, opening and closing the cap.
So the thing cleaning the water leaves a trace too.

title: What the other 90% is
body: The team looked for 7 common plastics. They made up only ~10% of the nanoparticles found.
What the rest is, and how it affects health, is still being studied.
This isn't a reason to panic. It means we can finally count them.
